title: Lazy Propagation
tagline: Range updates in O(log n) by deferring work until a node is actually visited.

intuition.analogy: A manager told 'give everyone on your team a raise' doesn't immediately walk to each desk. They note 'pending: +10% for my team' and only push it down when someone actually asks about a specific sub-team.
paragraphs: A plain segment tree updates one element at a time. To add a value to a whole RANGE without touching every leaf, lazy propagation stores a pending update at each node and applies it only when necessary.

When a range update fully covers a node, you update that node's aggregate and stash the pending delta in its 'lazy' tag instead of descending. Later, when a query or update needs the node's children, you 'push down' the stored delta first.
This keeps both range updates and range queries at O(log n). The bookkeeping — applying a tag to a node's value and propagating it to children correctly — is the part to internalise.
intuition.keyIdea: Store a pending update on fully-covered nodes; push it to children only when you must descend.

steps.title: Add a lazy tag
steps.detail: Each node has a pending value (e.g. 'add x to this whole range') not yet pushed to children.

steps.title: Apply on full cover
steps.detail: When a range update fully covers a node, adjust its aggregate (e.g. sum += x · rangeLen) and add x to its lazy tag; do not recurse.

steps.title: Push down before descending
steps.detail: Before recursing into children (for a partial update or query), apply the node's lazy tag to both children and clear it.

complexity.timeReason: Full-cover nodes stop recursion; only O(log n) boundary nodes are split.
complexity.spaceReason: An extra lazy array parallel to the tree.

pitfalls: Always push down before recursing into children, or stale values leak.
The tag must combine correctly (adds accumulate; assignments overwrite).
Scale aggregates by the segment length when the update is additive.

dryRun.input: Add 5 to range [0,3] on a size-8 array, then query [2,2]
dryRun.clickMoment: The range update never touched the individual leaves — it parked '+5' on node [0,3]. Only the later query forced that +5 to trickle down exactly where it was needed.
